turns.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that brought you in to see me today?

No matter how much I rest, I feel completely drained and I just can’t keep up at work anymore. My concentration is shot, and even on days when I sleep in, I still feel wiped out and unable to focus on what I’m doing.
Along with the fatigue and poor concentration, have you been feeling persistently down or hopeless, or more worried and tense than usual most days?

Yeah, most days I wake up feeling really low and hopeless, like there’s this heavy weight on my chest that doesn’t let up, even when nothing specific is going wrong. It’s been like that pretty consistently for at least a year, maybe longer.
In addition to feeling low and hopeless, do you also find yourself feeling excessively anxious or worried about many different things most days, and is it hard to control or turn those worries off?

Yeah, I spend a lot of time worrying, mostly about work—making mistakes, being watched or judged, that kind of thing—and once my mind gets going it’s really hard to shut it off. I’ll lie in bed with my thoughts spinning about what I did wrong or what people think of me, even when I’m trying to rest or have cut back on other things.

Over the past year, have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy most of the time, or do you still have moments where your mood lifts and you can enjoy things when you’re distracted from your worries?

Over the past year I’ve mostly lost interest in the stuff I used to enjoy, like jogging or tinkering with my Raspberry Pi projects—they just don’t appeal to me anymore. Even when I try to distract myself, it’s more like I’m going through the motions or just scrolling on my phone, and the low, heavy feeling doesn’t really lift in any meaningful way.

Do you ever have sudden episodes where your anxiety spikes out of nowhere, with intense physical symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like you’re losing control or going to die, that peak within minutes and then gradually ease off?

I don’t really get sudden spikes like that out of nowhere. My anxiety feels more constant and tied to specific worries, and while I might notice my heart beating faster sometimes, it’s not like a big wave that peaks and then passes in a few minutes.
Thinking about your low mood and loss of interest versus your constant worries, which one do you feel is causing more of your day‑to‑day problems at work and in your life overall?

Honestly, the low mood and feeling completely drained cause more of the day‑to‑day problems, because they make it hard just to get through a shift or do anything when I’m home. The constant worrying piles on and makes it worse, but it feels like the hopeless, exhausted feeling is what really stops me from functioning.

Do your worries and anxiety on their own significantly interfere with your daily life—for example, making you avoid tasks, fall behind at work, or struggle to function—even on days when your mood and energy feel a bit better, or is the impairment almost entirely tied to feeling low and exhausted?

Even on days when my mood and energy are a bit better, the worries still mess with me a lot. I’ll second‑guess everything, avoid certain tasks, and it slows me down and leads to mistakes, though things get much worse on top of that when I’m feeling really low and exhausted.

Thinking back, did the persistent anxiety and worry start around the same time as your low mood and loss of interest, or were you an anxious, worrier type for many months or years before you became this depressed and drained?

They really seemed to ramp up around the same time as the low mood and losing interest in things, after the big electronic record change and when I started picking up extra shifts and classes. Before that I had normal stress, but not this kind of constant, intrusive worry that’s hard to shut off.

Over the past year, have there been at least two straight weeks when you still felt anxious and worried but your mood was not clearly low or hopeless and you could enjoy things somewhat again, or have the low, heavy mood and loss of interest basically been present the whole time whenever the anxiety has been bad?

There was a stretch late last summer when my mood didn’t feel quite as low and I could enjoy things a bit more, but I was still really anxious and worrying a lot. Aside from brief periods like that where I felt more numb than deeply sad, the heavy low mood and loss of interest have pretty much been there most of the time whenever the anxiety has been bad.

If you imagine your anxiety staying the same but your mood, energy, and interest returning to normal, versus your mood improving only a little but your anxiety and worry dropping way down, which change do you think would help your day‑to‑day functioning more right now?

If my mood, energy, and interest went back to normal while the anxiety stayed the same, I think that would help my functioning more. I feel like if I wasn’t so drained and hopeless, I could keep up with my shifts, focus better, and maybe get back to my classes and hobbies, even if I was still pretty worried a lot of the time.
